methodology: Explicit artist-level decisions approved during the Songs for Self taxonomy review. Overrides outrank broad external tags, remain visible in genre_source and genre_evidence, and must include a rationale and evidence trail.

Iron & Wine.rationale: American indie-folk and singer-songwriter work is not World music.

The Mountain Goats.rationale: American indie-folk and folk-rock work is not World music.

Smash Mouth.rationale: American alternative/ska rock is not World music; a reggae tag alone does not override the artist's rock catalog.

Old Crow Medicine Show.rationale: American bluegrass, old-time, and Americana belong in Country rather than World.

Josh Ritter.rationale: American singer-songwriter and folk-rock work is not World music.

Streetlight Manifesto.rationale: Ska punk and punk rock map to the requested Rock family.

Self Esteem.rationale: Self Esteem's pop, art-pop, and electronic-pop catalog maps to the requested Pop family.

Pogo.rationale: Pogo's plunderphonics, deep-house, and glitch-hop work maps to Electronic.

Working for a Nuclear Free City.rationale: The user's reviewed placement and the artist's electronic/indietronica profile support Electronic.

Panama Wedding.rationale: The user's reviewed placement and indietronica/electropop evidence support Electronic.

Nico Segal.rationale: The user's reviewed placement and the Chance the Rapper collaboration catalog support Hip-hop.

Narada Nutcracker Performers.rationale: The catalog entries are arrangements of Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker ballet and map to Classical.

Camille.rationale: The catalog's existing chanson evidence maps this contemporary French singer to Pop.

Yuno Miles.rationale: MusicBrainz and Shazam both identify the artist as comedy hip-hop or Hip-Hop/Rap.

The Weepies.rationale: AllMusic identifies the duo as folk-pop, contemporary singer-songwriter, and indie folk.

Yeasayer.rationale: AllMusic's primary genre and styles place the band in indie and alternative rock.

Youth Lagoon.rationale: AllMusic groups the project under Pop/Rock with dream-pop, indie-rock, and neo-psychedelia styles.

Adam Green.rationale: AllMusic identifies anti-folk and alternative folk as core styles.

Mapei.rationale: AllMusic describes Mapei as a left-field pop artist spanning alternative R&B and rap.

Sungazer.rationale: The band's documented blend is jazz fusion with electronics and progressive rock.

Ted Hawkins.rationale: AllMusic identifies Hawkins under Blues and R&B, with soul-blues and acoustic-blues styles.

Todrick Hall.rationale: The requested taxonomy has no stage-and-screen family; the catalog's songs map best to Pop.

Bag Raiders.rationale: AllMusic identifies Electronic as the primary genre, with alternative dance and house styles.

Dan Deacon.rationale: AllMusic identifies Deacon as an electronic musician and experimental composer.

Fanfare Ciocarlia.rationale: The Romanian Romani brass band is represented in Rough Guide world-music collections and matches the Songlines-oriented World definition.

Frédéric Chopin.rationale: Chopin is a canonical Romantic-era classical composer.

Juan Gabriel.rationale: AllMusic identifies Latin pop and mariachi as core styles; the broad family is Pop.

People Under The Stairs.rationale: AllMusic identifies the duo under Rap with underground and West Coast rap styles.

Photay.rationale: AllMusic identifies Photay as an electronic musician working in IDM and experimental electronic music.

Quantic.rationale: AllMusic identifies Electronic first and documents broken-beat, house, and jazz-house work.

Shearwater.rationale: AllMusic identifies Shearwater as a Pop/Rock act with indie- and alternative-rock styles.

Great Big Sea.rationale: The Newfoundland band's contemporary performances blend Celtic and traditional material with modern folk-rock.

Young Dubliners.rationale: AllMusic identifies the Los Angeles band as Celtic folk-rock; Rock is the requested broad family.

Ennio Morricone.rationale: The requested taxonomy has no stage-and-screen family; Morricone's orchestral film scores map best to Classical.

Buck Meek.rationale: AllMusic identifies alt-country and indie folk as core styles and describes the solo work as country-inflected.

Carsick Cars.rationale: The catalog and AllMusic album evidence place the guitar band under Pop/Rock and noise-oriented indie rock.

J-Zone.rationale: AllMusic identifies J-Zone under Rap with underground, alternative, and East Coast styles.

Beatrice Dillon.rationale: AllMusic identifies Dillon under Electronic and Avant-Garde, led by experimental techno.

Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross.rationale: The requested taxonomy lacks stage-and-screen; the duo's electronic and ambient score work maps best to Experimental.

Axel Boman.rationale: The artist catalog and existing metadata consistently identify house and electronic dance music.

Beats Antique.rationale: The modern production-led catalog maps to Electronic, while regional influences remain in the detailed label.

Blue Scholars.rationale: The duo's rap catalog and artist tags map directly to Hip-hop.

Buraka Som Sistema.rationale: The production-led kuduro and moombahton catalog maps to Electronic.

Compay Segundo.rationale: The Cuban trova and son repertoire is a positive regional World assignment.

Dawn of Midi.rationale: The acoustic trio's experimental jazz and minimalist catalog maps to Jazz.

Dorothy Masuka.rationale: The South African regional repertoire is a positive World assignment, retaining jazz in the detailed label.

Emancipator.rationale: The instrumental, sample-based downtempo catalog maps directly to Electronic.

Fairuz.rationale: The Lebanese and Arabic repertoire is a positive regional World assignment.

Frente Cumbiero.rationale: The Colombian cumbia catalog is a positive regional World assignment.

Hans Zimmer.rationale: The requested taxonomy has no stage-and-screen family; the orchestral score catalog maps best to Classical.

Ibibio Sound Machine.rationale: The Nigerian Ibibio-language Afrobeat catalog is a positive regional World assignment.

Moondog.rationale: Existing minimalist evidence and the avant-garde catalog map directly to Experimental.

Mux Mool.rationale: Existing intelligent-dance-music evidence maps directly to Electronic.

Jesse Welles.rationale: The five playlist songs are contemporary American protest songs led by voice and acoustic guitar, mapping to Modern Folk.

The End of America.rationale: The trio's official biography and catalog describe a harmony-led indie-folk and folk-pop band.

Bitter:Sweet.rationale: The Los Angeles duo's catalog is consistently described as trip hop and electronica.

Mabe Fratti.rationale: The cello, voice, improvisation, and electronics catalog is explicitly avant-garde and experimental.

Nubya Garcia.rationale: Garcia is a jazz saxophonist and bandleader whose wider dub and club influences remain secondary.

Rudresh Mahanthappa.rationale: The artist's official biography identifies him as a leading contemporary jazz saxophonist and composer.

Seckou Keita.rationale: The Senegalese kora repertoire has positive regional evidence and three Songlines Music Awards, satisfying the project's World standard.

Penguin Cafe Orchestra.rationale: The ensemble's hybrid of avant-pop, chamber music, minimalism, and folk sits best in Experimental.

Connor Price.rationale: The Canadian rapper's official storefront biography and catalog classify the work as Hip-Hop/Rap.

Wheelchair Sports Camp.rationale: The band's own press biography calls it a hip-hop outfit, with live jazz instrumentation retained as a secondary label.

Robert Schumann.rationale: Schumann is a canonical Romantic-era classical composer; work-level dates remain separate from this genre decision.

The Piano Guys.rationale: The catalog's existing crossover evidence and instrumental classical arrangements map best to Classical under the requested taxonomy.

Adrian Crowley.rationale: Crowley's official biography and catalog center poetic singer-songwriter work rooted in folk traditions.

Andy Akiho.rationale: Akiho's official biography identifies his commissioned chamber and orchestral work as contemporary classical composition.

Ayub Ogada.rationale: Real World Records documents Ogada's Luo repertoire, indigenous instruments, WOMAD history, and Kenyan traditional sources.

Baaba Maal.rationale: Maal's Pulaar-language Senegalese repertoire and documented West African traditional roots provide positive World evidence.

Barker.rationale: The Ostgut Ton catalog places Barker's releases in the Berlin electronic and techno context.

Bellowhead.rationale: The band's official biography and catalog document an English folk ensemble arranging sea shanties, dance tunes, and traditional repertoire.

Bill Monroe & His Blue Grass Boys.rationale: The Bluegrass and Country Music Halls of Fame identify Monroe and the Blue Grass Boys as the defining bluegrass country ensemble.

Blockhead.rationale: AllMusic identifies Blockhead as a New York beatmaker producing abstract hip-hop for solo and rap catalogs.

Emahoy Tsege Mariam Gebru.rationale: The Ethiopian composer's regional piano language and inclusion in Rough Guide Ethiopian collections provide positive World evidence; the detailed label preserves the classical component.

Getatchew Mekurya.rationale: AllMusic identifies Mekurya as an Ethiopian jazz saxophonist and an early African-jazz figure.

Hanggai.rationale: The Inner Mongolian repertoire uses throat singing and traditional instruments alongside rock, providing positive regional World evidence.

Gazapizm.rationale: The artist catalog explicitly classifies Gazapizm as Turkish Hip-Hop/Rap.

Alex Gaudino.rationale: The Italian DJ and producer's catalog is documented as Italo-house and dance music.

Anomalie.rationale: Anomalie's production-led project explicitly combines electronic production with jazz and classical harmony.

CunninLynguists.rationale: The group's catalog is explicitly categorized as underground Hip-Hop/Rap.

Doomtree.rationale: Doomtree's official biography and catalog identify the Minneapolis collective as rap and hip-hop.

Johann Strauss II.rationale: Strauss is a canonical Romantic-era classical composer; work-level dates remain separate from this genre decision.

Johannes Brahms.rationale: Brahms is a canonical Romantic-era classical composer; work-level dates remain separate from this genre decision.

Jonny Greenwood.rationale: The playlist tracks are score compositions; the requested taxonomy lacks stage-and-screen, so the orchestral and contemporary-classical work maps best to Classical.

Auntie Flo.rationale: Brownswood documents an electronic producer fusing field recordings and global influences; production method, not nationality, supports Electronic.

Australian Art Orchestra.rationale: The ensemble's official biography explicitly locates its improvisational, cross-cultural practice in the evolving jazz tradition.

BAYNK.rationale: The New Zealand producer's catalog is explicitly electronic, with future-bass and house styles.

Ben Harper And The Innocent Criminals.rationale: The band catalog centers guitar-led rock while retaining its blues, soul, folk, and reggae influences as detail.

Bent Knee.rationale: The Boston band is consistently documented as art rock with progressive and experimental approaches.

Big Head Todd and The Monsters.rationale: The band's official history describes blues-drenched rock and a long rock-radio catalog.

Casey MQ.rationale: The producer's official biography and catalog identify electronic pop and production as the center of the project.

Chiwoniso.rationale: The Zimbabwean mbira repertoire has direct regional and traditional-instrument evidence.

Cory Wong.rationale: The catalog and AllMusic biography center funk, R&B, and soul-jazz groove rather than broad rock geography.

Daniel Johnston.rationale: Johnston's voice-led, home-recorded singer-songwriter catalog maps best to Modern Folk while retaining its outsider and lo-fi qualities.

Deca.rationale: The artist and label biographies identify Deca as a rapper and producer working in instrumental hip-hop.

DURRY.rationale: The Minneapolis sibling band describes itself as indie rock and presents a guitar-band catalog.

Édith Piaf.rationale: Piaf is a canonical French popular chanson singer; the broad requested family is Pop.

Foxygen.rationale: The duo's classic-rock and psychedelic catalog maps to Rock while retaining experimental pop as detail.

FORQ.rationale: AllMusic and the band's own material identify an improvising electric jazz-fusion quartet.

Jlin.rationale: The Gary producer's official publishing biography and catalog center electronic footwork and experimental composition.

Hermitude.rationale: The Australian duo's official biography identifies an electronic act with hip-hop roots and electronic soundscapes.

Gyptian.rationale: The Jamaican roots-reggae and dancehall catalog provides positive regional and genre evidence for World.

Indigo De Souza.rationale: The North Carolina singer-songwriter's catalog is consistently documented as indie and alternative rock.

Joe Cuba.rationale: The Puerto Rican New York bandleader's bilingual salsa and Latin-boogaloo catalog provides positive regional genre evidence.

Caught A Ghost.rationale: The catalog's soul vocals and rhythm-and-blues foundation map best to R&B/Soul/Blues, with electronic production retained as detail.

Indian Calling.rationale: The playlist recordings are presented as Native American flute and traditional instrumental repertoire.

Londrelle.rationale: The catalog combines spoken-word affirmations with neo-soul and R&B production; the requested taxonomy has no spoken-word family.

2nd South Carolina String Band.rationale: The ensemble performs documented nineteenth-century American camp, minstrel, and string-band repertoire.

888.rationale: The Denver trio's guitar-band catalog maps to alternative and indie rock.

Alexis Harte.rationale: Harte's acoustic, lyric-led singer-songwriter work maps to Modern Folk.

Bill Wurtz.rationale: The melodic song catalog is built from compact pop forms, even though its harmony, editing, and humor are unconventional.

Boiled In Lead.rationale: The Minneapolis group's electric rhythm section and folk-punk presentation map to Rock while preserving its international folk repertoire as detail.

Dan Reeder.rationale: Reeder's home-recorded, acoustic, lyric-forward work is contemporary singer-songwriter folk.

Daniel Pemberton.rationale: The playlist selections are screen scores; without a stage-and-screen family, their composed orchestral function maps best to Classical.

Enter The Haggis.rationale: The Canadian band's amplified Celtic and folk-rock catalog maps to Rock.

Guerilla Toss.rationale: The group's guitar-band and dance-punk catalog maps to Rock, with experimental practice retained as detail.

In Love With a Ghost.rationale: The producer-led instrumental catalog uses electronic beat production associated with chillhop and lo-fi electronic music.

Jay Warren.rationale: The vocal catalog and production style map to contemporary R&B and soul.

Julie Andrews.rationale: The requested taxonomy lacks stage-and-screen; Andrews's popular vocal and show-tune recordings map most legibly to Pop.

Julie Feeney.rationale: Feeney's composed, theatrical vocal catalog is consistently framed as art and chamber pop.

Michael Franti.rationale: Franti's band-led catalog mixes alternative rock with reggae and hip-hop; Rock is the most stable top-level home.

Paper Bird.rationale: The Colorado ensemble's acoustic harmony and Americana repertoire map to Modern Folk.

Phosphorescent.rationale: Matthew Houck's lyric-led indie-folk and Americana catalog maps to Modern Folk.

Ruth Pelham.rationale: Pelham's community singing and traditional/topical folk practice maps to Traditional Folk.

SAULT.rationale: The collective's catalog centers neo-soul, funk, and contemporary R&B.

Sergio Mendes & Brasil '66.rationale: The Brazilian ensemble's bossa nova and samba repertoire provides positive regional genre evidence for World.

Stan Rogers.rationale: Rogers's original, lyric-led Canadian folk songs map to Modern Folk rather than anonymous traditional repertoire.

The Bellas.rationale: The Pitch Perfect vocal soundtrack performances use contemporary pop repertoire and arrangements.

the bird and the bee.rationale: The duo's melodic electronic and lounge-influenced catalog maps to Pop.

The Felice Brothers.rationale: The Catskills group's roots-oriented Americana and folk-rock songwriting maps to Modern Folk.

The Hollyfelds.rationale: The Denver band's catalog is country and Americana, with twang-forward ensemble arrangements.

The Saw Doctors.rationale: The Irish guitar band's catalog maps to Celtic and folk rock.

Tony Exum Jr.rationale: Exum's saxophone-led catalog is contemporary and smooth jazz.

Vulfmon.rationale: Jack Stratton's Vulfmon catalog centers funk rhythm, soul, and jazz-funk production.

Youngblood Brass Band.rationale: The ensemble's brass-band instrumentation and improvisation map to Jazz, with hip-hop influence retained as detail.

Yung Spinach.rationale: The vocal delivery, beat construction, and catalog context map to Hip-hop, even where the presentation is comic.
